name: ExLlamaV3
notable_features: EXL3 quantization is a streamlined variant of QTIP (Cornell RelaxML): Hessians computed on the fly plus a fused Viterbi kernel make conversion a single pass — minutes for small models, hours for 70B+ on one consumer GPU.
2-8 bit KV/attention cache quantization, so the cache is not stuck at fp16.
Flexible tensor-parallel and expert-parallel inference aimed at consumer hardware, not multi-node racks.
Deliberate CPU offload feature for running large MoE models with limited GPU resources, with AVX2 and AVX512 paths.
Triton-based attention, cache and recurrent kernels — the package does not import without triton-windows on Windows.
Transformers plugin plus an OpenAI-compatible API via TabbyAPI; very broad HF architecture coverage including multimodal (DeepSeek V4, GLM 4.7/5.3 Flash, Qwen 3.5, Gemma 4, MiMo).
Vendors Marlin and Flash Linear Attention kernels (chunked linear-attention prefill under exllamav3/vendor/fla).
hardware_caveats: NVIDIA-first: requires PyTorch with CUDA 12.4+ (flavor extras cu124/cu126/cu128/cu129/cu130/cu132). Minimum torch 2.6.0. No ROCm, Metal, or Vulkan path documented.
On Windows the triton-windows package is a declared dependency — attention, cache and recurrent kernels are Triton, and ExLlamaV3 will not import without it.

The PyPI package ships no prebuilt extension: it requires the CUDA toolkit and build prerequisites (VS Build Tools on Windows, gcc on Linux, python-dev headers). Prebuilt wheels exist on the releases page.

Isolated builds (`uv sync`, `pip install .`) do not see your installed torch and instead JIT-compile the extension on first import, which takes minutes once per torch version. Use `--no-build-isolation` or a release wheel to avoid that.
If you have both an AMD and an NVIDIA GPU, llama.cpp-style backend selection issues do not apply here, but multi-GPU assumes CUDA; tensor- and expert-parallel are NVIDIA topologies.
Some listed architectures are explicitly unsupported: Gemma 4 E2B/E4B (the README notes them unsupported), and MiMo-V2.6-Flash has no audio support.
best_for: Current-generation NVIDIA consumer cards: best-quality low-bit quants plus explicit MoE expert/tensor parallelism for machines that are not a datacenter.
Fitting a large MoE model into a single card with CPU offload for the leftover experts.
Single-user interactive decode speed where cache precision matters (2-8 bit cache).
Architecture coverage: the HF list is the broadest of any engine here.
Fast one-pass quantization from HF safetensors to EXL3.
avoid_for: CPU-only inference — the CPU path exists but only as an offload target for MoE, not as the primary engine.
Simplicity: build-time CUDA/Triton setup is real work compared to llama.cpp or ONNX paths.
Serving workloads that need paged KV across many concurrent users; the generator does dynamic batching but the project is single-user oriented.
notes: EXL3 is a different format from EXL2 — no checkpoint compatibility between them. BUILD COST, the only published figure for this engine and a genuinely different pattern from vLLM's or TensorRT-LLM's: the PyPI package 'does not contain a prebuilt extension', and both uv sync and pip install build 'in an isolated environment where your torch is not visible, so they install the extension sources and compile them at first import (JIT, a few minutes once per torch version)'. So the compile is JITTED AT FIRST IMPORT rather than performed by an install step, and the repeat condition is precise and favourable: 'a few minutes ONCE PER TORCH VERSION' - not per model, not per configuration. Documented workarounds: pip install --no-build-isolation . in an environment that already has torch, or a release wheel. Build inputs are declared as CUDA flavor extras cu124/cu126/cu128/cu129/cu130/cu132 against a minimum of torch 2.6.0 and CUDA 12.4. FEATURE AXES: continuous batching, speculative decoding and multimodal are all confirmed YES by the vendor's own README bullet ('Generation - Continuous, dynamic batching, speculative decoding, multimodal support'), and expert parallelism plus 2-8 bit cache quantization are present. Note for anyone comparing server capability: ExLlamaV3 SHIPS NO SERVER - the README names TabbyAPI as 'the official and recommended backend server', so multi-model and structured-output capability at the engine level cannot be answered from this project and belongs to a different repository.
